steps.subject: [MC][ELF] Make linked-to symbol name part of ELFSectionKey

evidence: Directly changes MC ELF section identity based on linked symbols and updates the exact AArch64 patchable-function-entry test family.
A bad linked-symbol/section association is plausibly relevant to later symbol-reference emission, though the diff does not directly modify emitXRayTable or MCSymbolRefExpr construction.
features: aarch64-patchable-function-entry, build:make, linked-symbol-handling, mc-elf-section-key, mc-symbol-identity, path:llvm/include/llvm/MC
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes ELF section uniquing so that the linked-to symbol name is part of MCContext's ELFSectionKey. Consequently, sections with the same name, group, and unique ID but different SHF_LINK_ORDER targets are no longer merged. It also adjusts renameELFSection's key use for debug sections, which are documented here as not using SHF_LINK_ORDER, and updates AArch64 patchable-function-entry tests to expect each patchable-entry section to link to its own function symbol.
Changed symbols: MCContext::getELFSection; MCContext::renameELFSection; MCContext::ELFSectionKey; MCSectionELF
Behavioral change: ELF section identity changes from effectively (section name, group name, unique ID) to (section name, group name, linked-to symbol name, unique ID).; Calls to MCContext::getELFSection now distinguish otherwise-identical sections by LinkedToSym->getName().; AArch64 __patchable_function_entries output for a second function is expected to use that function's symbol (for example, f2 rather than f1) as the linked-to symbol.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64; MCSymbolELF; LinkedToSym; ELF section uniquing
Reproducer link: Directly modifies llvm/test/CodeGen/AArch64/patchable-function-entry.ll.; Directly modifies llvm/test/CodeGen/AArch64/patchable-function-entry-bti.ll.; Both tests exercise __patchable_function_entries sections and verify their function-symbol linkage.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM MC ELF section creation and uniquing; AArch64 patchable-function-entry lowering/output; MC symbol and section handling
Causal explanation: This is the strongest candidate because it directly changes the MC-layer identity of linked ELF sections and updates the exact AArch64 patchable-function-entry test family implicated by the issue. Incorrectly merging sections associated with different function symbols can propagate an incorrect linked symbol through later assembly emission, plausibly producing invalid symbol/reference state in the XRay or patchable-entry path. The retrieved hunks do not directly modify MCSymbolRefExpr, AArch64AsmPrinter, or emitXRayTable, so the specific assertion mechanism is inferred from the corrected section-to-symbol association rather than shown directly.
Causal confidence: 0.90
Build risk: Updates existing AArch64 CodeGen tests, providing targeted regression coverage for the changed section linkage.; Changes MCContext key construction and therefore affects ELF section uniquing globally for callers using LinkedToSym.; Retrieved diff coverage is incomplete: 37 hunks were omitted and raw diff content was truncated.

top_candidates.subject: [llvm][CodeGen][aarch64] Add contiguous prefetch intrinsics for SVE.
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Adds AArch64 SVE contiguous-prefetch instruction-selection patterns and extends SVE indexed-address selection so it can derive a memory vector type not only from MemSDNode operations but also from the aarch64_sve_prf intrinsic. The change removes the prior unconditional MemSDNode assertion in SelectAddrModeIndexedSVE and adds SVE prefetch code-generation tests.
Changed symbols: AArch64DAGToDAGISel::SelectAddrModeIndexedSVE; getPackedVectorTypeFromPredicateType; getMemVTFromNode; sve_prefetch; int_aarch64_sve_prf
Behavioral change: SelectAddrModeIndexedSVE now accepts an SVE prefetch INTRINSIC_VOID root in addition to a MemSDNode root, rather than asserting that every root is a MemSDNode.; For aarch64_sve_prf, the indexed-address scale is inferred from the scalable predicate width by constructing the corresponding packed scalable integer vector type.; New TableGen patterns select register-plus-immediate, register-plus-register, and base-only forms of contiguous SVE prefetch instructions.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64 target overlap; The changed assertion is "Invalid node." in SelectionDAG address matching, not the reported MCSymbolRefExpr Symbol assertion.; No retrieved hunk references MCSymbolRefExpr, MCSymbol, Symbol, emitXRayTable, or XRay.
Reproducer link: The added tests exercise llvm.aarch64.sve.prf.nxv16i1 and check emitted prfb instructions.; The issue reproducer is described as using XRay patchable-function-entry metadata; no such metadata or function-entry handling appears in the retrieved hunks.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64 SelectionDAG instruction selection; AArch64 SVE TableGen instruction patterns; Not AArch64 Assembly Printer, XRay table emission, or MC symbol/reference handling
Causal explanation: This commit is AArch64-specific and changes an assertion-bearing code path, but the affected path is SVE prefetch address selection before assembly emission. The reported failure concerns MCSymbolRefExpr/Symbol during AArch64 XRay table emission. The retrieved code neither creates nor emits MC symbol references and has no XRay or patchable-function-entry interaction, so there is no direct evidence that it can cause the issue.
Causal confidence: 0.06
Build risk: Changes both C++ SelectionDAG code and AArch64 TableGen patterns, so failures could affect AArch64 SVE instruction selection.; Adds llc/FileCheck coverage for contiguous SVE prefetch encodings and indexed-address cases.; Retrieved candidate diff is incomplete: 42 hunks were omitted and raw diff retrieval was truncated.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This changes AArch64 load/store post-index optimization around the stack pointer. AArch64LoadStoreOpt now rejects the optimization for Windows functions requiring unwind entries and, when the optimized base register is SP, rejects candidate updates if an intervening instruction may load or store memory. The accompanying MIR test ensures a stack store is not converted into a premature SP post-increment.
Changed symbols: AArch64LoadStoreOpt::findMatchingUpdateInsnForward; MCAsmInfo
Behavioral change: Disables the SP update-folding optimization for Windows CFI functions that need unwind-table entries.; Prevents SP post-increment folding across any intervening load or store, preserving the original stack-addressing lifetime.; Adds an AArch64 MIR regression test checking that a store is not emitted as "[sp], #16" before the explicit stack restoration.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64
Reproducer link: The added reproducer concerns premature stack-pointer popping during AArch64 load/store optimization.; No XRay, patchable-function-entry metadata, emitXRayTable, MCSymbolRefExpr, or Symbol assertion behavior appears in the retrieved hunks.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64LoadStoreOpt; AArch64 machine-instruction optimization; Windows CFI/unwind handling
Causal explanation: The commit is AArch64-specific, but it changes a machine-level stack-address optimization rather than assembly-printer XRay table emission or MC symbol-reference construction. The use of MCAsmInfo is limited to checking Windows CFI behavior. The retrieved evidence therefore provides no direct path to an MCSymbolRefExpr Symbol assertion from emitXRayTable.
Causal confidence: 0.04
Build risk: Adds a direct llc MIR regression test for the altered optimization.; Introduces an MCAsmInfo dependency into the AArch64 load/store optimizer.; No visible regression test exercises XRay table emission or MC symbol-reference assertions.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit implements AAPCS passing of scalable SVE vectors by reference in the AArch64 SelectionDAG lowering path. It recognizes indirect CCValAssign locations, sizes indirect arguments according to their location type, loads indirect formal arguments, spills indirect call arguments into SVE stack objects, prevents tail calls when indirect SVE arguments require stack storage, removes the previous fatal rejection of the SVE vector calling convention, and adds an SVE store pattern and no-tail-call tests.
Changed symbols: AArch64TargetLowering::LowerFormalArguments; AArch64TargetLowering::CCAssignFnForCall; AArch64TargetLowering::isEligibleForTailCallOptimization; AArch64TargetLowering::LowerCall; AArch64SVEInstrInfo.td
Behavioral change: Scalable SVE vectors assigned with CCValAssign::Indirect are passed and received through pointers rather than being rejected or treated as direct values.; Indirect scalable-vector call arguments are spilled to TargetStackID::SVEVector stack objects before calls.; Tail-call optimization is disabled when an argument is indirectly passed, because stack allocation is required.; The AArch64_SVE_VectorCall calling convention is no longer unconditionally rejected with a fatal error.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64
Reproducer link: The added tests exercise scalable SVE vector calls and required non-tail-call stack setup.; No retrieved test or hunk mentions XRay, emitXRayTable, MCSymbolRefExpr, __patchable_function_entries, or symbol-reference assertions.

new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..ca29e15697fe
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/CodeGen/AArch64/sve-callbyref-notailcall.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@
+; Because some arguments are passed by reference (through stack),
+; the compiler should not do tail-call optimization.
+; RUN: llc -mtriple=aarch64 -mattr=+sve < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+; CHECK-LABEL: caller:
+; CHECK:       addvl sp, sp, #-[[STACKSIZE:[0-9]+]]
+; CHECK-NOT:   addvl sp
+; CHECK:       bl callee
+; CHECK:       addvl sp, sp, #[[STACKSIZE]]
+; CHECK:       ret
+define <vscale x 16 x i8> @caller(<vscale x 16 x i8> %v) {
+  %1 = tail call <vscale x 16 x i8> @callee(<vscale x 16 x i8> %v, <vscale x 16 x i8> %v, <vscale x 16 x i8> %v, <vscale x 16 x i8> %v, <vscale x 16 x i8> %v, <vscale x 16 x i8> %v, <vscale x 16 x i8> %v, <vscale x 16 x i8> %v, <vscale x 16 x i8> %v)
+  ret <vscale x 16 x i8> %1
+}
+
+declare <vscale x 16 x i8> @callee(<vscale x 16 x i8>, <vscale x 16 x i8>, <vscale x 16 x i8>, <vscale x 16 x i8>, <vscale x 16 x i8>, <vscale x 16 x i8>, <vscale x 16 x i8>, <vscale x 16 x i8>, <vscale x 16 x i8>)
+
+; CHECK-LABEL: caller_pred:
+; CHECK:       addvl sp, sp, #-[[STACKSIZE:[0-9]+]]
+; CHECK-NOT:   addvl sp
+; CHECK:       bl callee_pred
+; CHECK:       addvl sp, sp, #[[STACKSIZE]]
+; CHECK:       ret
+define <vscale x 16 x i1> @caller_pred(<vscale x 16 x i1> %v) {
+  %1 = tail call <vscale x 16 x i1> @callee_pred(<vscale x 16 x i1> %v, <vscale x 16 x i1> %v, <vscale x 16 x i1> %v, <vscale x 16 x i1> %v, <vscale x 16 x i1> %v)
+  ret <vscale x 16 x i1> %1
+}
+
+declare <vscale x 16 x i1> @callee_pred(<vscale x 16 x i1>, <vscale x 16 x i1>, <vscale x 16 x i1>, <vscale x 16 x i1>, <vscale x 16 x i1>)

Summary: Changes AArch64 SelectionDAG comparison lowering to reuse an ANDS result and condition-code value when comparing an AND result against zero. It also recognizes ANDS as a masked shift amount in tryShiftAmountMod, replacing separate AND/TST-style sequences with combined flag-setting ANDS instructions where applicable.
Changed symbols: emitComparison; AArch64DAGToDAGISel::tryShiftAmountMod; isOpcWithIntImmediate; AArch64ISD::ANDS
Behavioral change: For signed comparisons of an AND result with zero, emitComparison creates an AArch64ISD::ANDS node, replaces uses of the original AND value with the ANDS result, and returns the ANDS condition-code result.; If the comparison input is already an AArch64ISD::ANDS node, emitComparison reuses its flags instead of creating another comparison sequence.; tryShiftAmountMod now accepts either ISD::AND or AArch64ISD::ANDS when recognizing a masked shift amount.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64 target overlap; No retrieved hunk references MCSymbolRefExpr, MCSymbol, Symbol, XRay, emitXRayTable, or an assembly-printer assertion.
Reproducer link: The tests cover integer AND/compare-to-zero, funnel shifts, and expected ands instruction emission.; No test or changed code handles XRay instrumentation or patchable-function-entry metadata.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64 SelectionDAG lowering; AArch64 DAG instruction selection; Not AArch64 Assembly Printer, XRay emission, or LLVM MC symbol/reference handling
Causal explanation: The commit can alter AArch64 machine instruction and condition-code generation, but all visible changes concern integer AND/ANDS lowering and shift masking. The issue signal is specifically an MC symbol-reference assertion during XRay table emission; no evidence in the retrieved hunks connects these DAG peepholes to XRay metadata lowering or MC symbol construction.
Causal confidence: 0.03
Build risk: Replaces DAG uses through DAG.ReplaceAllUsesWith, so the change affects users of matched AND nodes within the SelectionDAG.; Adds a dedicated peephole regression test and updates existing AArch64 assembly expectations from and/tst sequences to ands.; Retrieved coverage reports 32 omitted hunks, although the raw diff itself was not truncated.

+entry:
+  %0 = load %struct.anon*, %struct.anon** @ptr_wrapper, align 8
+  %result = getelementptr inbounds %struct.anon, %struct.anon* %0, i64 0, i32 1
+  %tobool2 = icmp ne i32 %mask, 0
+  br label %do.body
+
+do.body:                                          ; preds = %4, %entry
+; CHECK-LABEL: test_func_i32_two_uses:
+; CHECK: ands [[DSTREG:w[0-9]+]]
+; Usage #1

+; Usage #2

+  %bit.addr.0 = phi i32 [ %bit, %entry ], [ %shl, %4 ]
+  %retval1.0 = phi i32 [ 0, %entry ], [ %retval1.1, %4 ]
+  %and = and i32 %bit.addr.0, %in
+  %tobool = icmp eq i32 %and, 0
+  %not.tobool = xor i1 %tobool, true
+  %inc = zext i1 %not.tobool to i32
+  %retval1.1 = add nuw nsw i32 %retval1.0, %inc
+  %1 = xor i1 %tobool, true
+  %2 = or i1 %tobool2, %1
+  %dummy = and i32 %mask, %in
+  %use_and = icmp eq i32 %and, %dummy
+  %dummy_or = or i1 %use_and, %2
+  br i1 %dummy_or, label %3, label %4
+

+  store i32* null, i32** %result, align 8
+  br label %4
+

+  %shl = shl i32 %bit.addr.0, 1
+  %tobool6 = icmp eq i32 %shl, 0
+  br i1 %tobool6, label %do.end, label %do.body
+
+do.end:                                           ; preds = %4
+  ret i32 %retval1.1
+}

+  %bit.addr.0 = phi i64 [ %bit, %entry ], [ %shl, %4 ]

+  %tobool = icmp eq i64 %and, 0
+  %not.tobool = xor i1 %tobool, true
+  %inc = zext i1 %not.tobool to i32
+  %retval1.1 = add nuw nsw i32 %retval1.0, %inc
+  %1 = xor i1 %tobool, true

top_candidates.subject: [AArch64][Fix] LdSt optimization generate premature stack-popping
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This AArch64 load/store optimizer fix restricts formation of post-index stack-pointer updates so that the optimizer does not move an SP increment across intervening memory operations. It also disables the SP optimization for Windows CFI functions requiring unwind-table entries, because moving the adjustment would require corresponding unwind/debug-information changes. A new MIR test checks that the stack adjustment remains a separate ADD rather than becoming a post-indexed store.
Changed symbols: AArch64LoadStoreOpt::findMatchingUpdateInsnForward; AArch64LoadStoreOpt; MCAsmInfo
Behavioral change: When optimizing an update based on SP, findMatchingUpdateInsnForward rejects candidate ranges containing an intervening instruction that may load or store memory.; For Windows CFI functions that need an unwind-table entry, the optimizer declines the SP post-increment transformation entirely.; The pass queries MCAsmInfo::usesWindowsCFI to enforce the unwind-information restriction.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64
Reproducer link: The new reproducer concerns premature stack popping around stack memory accesses and verifies separate SP adjustment code; it has no XRay or patchable-function-entry metadata.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64 load/store optimization; Windows CFI and unwind-information handling
Causal explanation: The change shares the AArch64 target and includes an MCAsmInfo query, but it operates on MachineInstr stack-pointer update folding rather than Assembly Printer emission or MC symbol-reference generation. The retrieved hunks contain no MCSymbolRefExpr, Symbol, XRay, emitXRayTable, or patchable-function-entry handling, so there is no evidence-backed route to the reported assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.02
Build risk: Adds an AArch64 MIR regression test run through llc starting before the AArch64 load/store optimizer.; Changes expected AArch64 assembly behavior by preventing a post-indexed SP store in the tested case.; Adds an MCAsmInfo include but does not alter MC symbol/reference APIs or XRay code in the retrieved hunks.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit strengthens MC handling of virtual sections, specifically ELF SHT_NOBITS and COFF IMAGE_SCN_CNT_UNINITIALIZED_DATA sections. It replaces fatal assembler failures for fixups and non-zero initializers with MCContext diagnostics, prevents instruction emission into virtual sections, and adds target-specific virtual-section-kind strings for clearer diagnostics.
Changed symbols: MCAssembler::writeSectionData; MCObjectStreamer::emitInstruction; MCSection::getVirtualSectionKind; MCSectionELF::getVirtualSectionKind; MCSectionCOFF::getVirtualSectionKind
Behavioral change: MCObjectStreamer::emitInstruction now rejects and returns without emitting an instruction when the current section is virtual.; MCAssembler::writeSectionData now reports MCContext errors, rather than immediately calling report_fatal_error, for fixups or non-zero initializers in virtual sections.; ELF and COFF virtual sections now identify themselves as SHT_NOBITS and IMAGE_SCN_CNT_UNINITIALIZED_DATA in diagnostics.
Assertion or trace link: MC subsystem; MCSymbolRefExpr and Symbol are present in the issue signal but are not modified by this commit
Reproducer link: The reported reproducer crashes while lowering AArch64 XRay patchable-function-entry metadata, not while emitting instructions into an SHT_NOBITS or COFF uninitialized-data section.
Pass or subsystem link: MC assembler; MC object streamer; ELF/COFF section emission
Causal explanation: The commit is in the MC layer, which is adjacent to symbol/reference handling implicated by the assertion, but its actual new invariant concerns contents of virtual sections. The retrieved hunks do not change MCSymbolRefExpr creation or validation, AArch64 assembly printing, XRay table emission, or patchable-function metadata lowering. It could only be involved if the XRay path emitted into a virtual section, for which no evidence is provided.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Changes common MC behavior for ELF and COFF object emission.; Introduces recoverable diagnostics and early return for invalid instruction emission in virtual sections.; No test hunk is visible in the retrieved evidence for these virtual-section diagnostics.

Summary: Makes `MCAsmInfo::UseIntegratedAssembler` default to true and removes now-redundant true assignments from AArch64 ELF, COFF, and Darwin MCAsmInfo constructors. For AArch64 ELF specifically, the effective setting remains true before and after this commit.
Changed symbols: MCAsmInfo::MCAsmInfo; AArch64MCAsmInfoELF::AArch64MCAsmInfoELF; MCAsmInfoCOFF::MCAsmInfoCOFF; MCAsmInfoDarwin::MCAsmInfoDarwin; UseIntegratedAssembler
Behavioral change: Changes the base `MCAsmInfo` default for `UseIntegratedAssembler` from false to true.; Removes target-specific constructor assignments that already set `UseIntegratedAssembler` to true.; Does not change the effective `UseIntegratedAssembler` value for AArch64 ELF, because its constructor set the value to true before the base default changed.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64; MC
Reproducer link: The issue is triggered by llc on AArch64 IR and fails in an MC-symbol-related assertion during XRay table assembly emission.; This candidate changes an MC assembly-configuration default, but the retrieved AArch64 ELF constructor shows no effective setting change for the affected target.; No retrieved hunk mentions XRay, emitXRayTable, patchable-function-entry metadata, MCSymbolRefExpr, or `MCSymbol`.
Pass or subsystem link: MCAsmInfo; AArch64 MC target description

// Write X as an (unsigned) LEB value at offset Offset in Stream, padded
// to allow patching.
static void writePatchableLEB(raw_pwrite_stream &Stream, uint32_t X,
                              uint64_t Offset) {
  uint8_t Buffer[5];
  unsigned SizeLen = encodeULEB128(X, Buffer, 5);
  assert(SizeLen == 5);
  Stream.pwrite((char *)Buffer, SizeLen, Offset);
}

// Write X as an signed LEB value at offset Offset in Stream, padded
// to allow patching.
static void writePatchableSLEB(raw_pwrite_stream &Stream, int32_t X,
                               uint64_t Offset) {
  uint8_t Buffer[5];
  unsigned SizeLen = encodeSLEB128(X, Buffer, 5);
  assert(SizeLen == 5);
  Stream.pwrite((char *)Buffer, SizeLen, Offset);
}

// Write X as a plain integer value at offset Offset in Stream.
static void writeI32(raw_pwrite_stream &Stream, uint32_t X, uint64_t Offset) {
  uint8_t Buffer[4];
  support::endian::write32le(Buffer, X);
  Stream.pwrite((char *)Buffer, sizeof(Buffer), Offset);
}

evidence: Changes AArch64 GlobalISel decisions by excluding debug-only uses from register-bank and instruction-selection logic.
This can affect generated machine code in debug-bearing inputs, but it does not touch the late AsmPrinter/XRay/MC-symbol failure path.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit updates AArch64 GlobalISel use-count and use-iteration logic to ignore debug-only machine-instruction uses. It replaces use_instructions with use_nodbg_instructions in AArch64RegisterBankInfo::getInstrMapping, replaces hasOneUse with hasOneNonDBGUse in getTestBitReg, and changes tryOptSelect's conditional-definition user scan to ignore debug users.
Changed symbols: AArch64RegisterBankInfo::getInstrMapping; getTestBitReg; AArch64InstructionSelector::tryOptSelect
Behavioral change: Register-bank mapping decisions now disregard DBG_VALUE and other debug-only uses when testing whether a virtual register has relevant users.; The instruction selector's test-bit optimization treats a register with one non-debug use as single-use even if debug instructions also reference it.; The optimized-select scan no longer considers debug-only users when locating the conditional-definition instruction.

Summary: Changes XRay sled emission for AArch64 to record version-2 sleds and changes AsmPrinter XRay-table emission to use PC-relative addresses on every non-MIPS target, including AArch64. The accompanying AArch64 XRay test changes expected table entries from absolute symbol addresses to expressions subtracting per-entry temporary labels.
Changed symbols: AArch64AsmPrinter::EmitSled; recordSled; AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable
Behavioral change: AArch64 XRay sleds are recorded with version 2 via recordSled(CurSled, MI, Kind, 2).; emitXRayTable changes PC-relative-address selection from x86-only to all non-MIPS targets, making AArch64 XRay-table entries PC-relative.; AArch64 XRay table assembly changes from absolute '.xword .Lxray_sled_N' entries to symbol-difference expressions such as '.xword .Lxray_sled_N-.LtmpN'.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64 Assembly Printer; emitXRayTable; MCSymbolRefExpr; Symbol assertion
Reproducer link: The issue reproduces on reduced AArch64 IR with XRay patchable-function-entry metadata.; This commit directly changes AArch64 XRay sled/table emission and the symbolic expressions emitted into that table.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64AsmPrinter; CodeGen AsmPrinter; XRay table emission; MC symbol/reference expression emission

In particular, switching AArch64 table entries to PC-relative symbol differences introduces new symbol-reference expressions during emitXRayTable, the subsystem named in the crash signal. The updated AArch64 XRay test confirms that the emitted representation changed to label-relative expressions, although the retrieved test does not cover the reported assertion or patchable-function-entry reproducer specifically.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Introduces an FPR16_lo AArch64 register class and operand, uses that restricted class in f16 indexed SIMD tied patterns, and teaches register-bank and register-pressure queries to recognize the new class. This constrains the register selection for the affected half-precision indexed patterns to the lower FPR16 subset.
Changed symbols: SIMDFPIndexedTiedPatterns; FPR16_lo; FPR16Op_lo; AArch64RegisterBankInfo::getRegBankFromRegClass; AArch64RegisterInfo::getRegPressureLimit
Behavioral change: Adds the FPR16_lo register class as a truncated lower subset of FPR16.; Adds FPR16Op_lo and substitutes it for FPR16Op in the affected f16 indexed SIMD tied instruction patterns.; Maps FPR16_lo-related classes in register-bank lookup and assigns FPR16_lo a register-pressure-limit handling case.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64 SIMD instruction selection; AArch64 register classes and register-bank mapping; Register pressure handling
Causal explanation: The candidate changes AArch64 register constraints and SIMD pattern selection, which can affect generated machine code, but it does not touch assembly printing, XRay table construction, MC symbol references, or patchable-function-entry metadata. The issue's MCSymbolRefExpr/Symbol assertion in emitXRayTable is therefore not supported by the retrieved change as a direct consequence.
Causal confidence: 0.02
Build risk: Moderate backend integration risk because a new TableGen register class must remain consistent with register-bank and pressure handling.; The retrieved hunks update both TableGen definitions and C++ consumers, reducing the risk of an immediately unrecognized register class.; No candidate-owned regression test is present in the retrieved hunks.; No retrieved evidence covers XRay instrumentation, XRay table emission, MC symbol handling, or the reported assertion path.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes AArch64 GlobalISel outgoing-call lowering for Darwin by removing a special AnyExt transformation for AExt-assigned stack arguments. The accompanying AArch64 calling-convention tests update expected MIR for stack-passed narrow arguments, varargs, and aggregate calls.
Changed symbols: OutgoingArgHandler; AArch64CallLowering; test_stack_ext_needed; test_varargs; caller_s128; i8i16caller
Behavioral change: Outgoing argument lowering no longer forcibly applies buildAnyExt to an AExt argument before stack assignment.; Sub-64-bit Darwin stack-argument lowering is expected to preserve the appropriate stored width and stack layout rather than uniformly widening via the removed special case.; Regression expectations are updated for normal AArch64 and iOS/Darwin GlobalISel calling-convention MIR, including narrow stack arguments and varargs.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64
Reproducer link: The tests exercise GlobalISel call argument lowering and Darwin stack layout; the issue reproducer instead involves XRay patchable-function-entry metadata and an Assembly Printer MCSymbolRefExpr assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64 GlobalISel; AArch64CallLowering; calling-convention stack argument lowering
Causal explanation: The commit is AArch64-specific, but its visible effect is limited to outgoing call argument extension and stack stores in GlobalISel. The retrieved evidence does not touch AsmPrinter, XRay, MCStreamer, MCSymbolRefExpr, or XRay table emission. A malformed machine function could theoretically propagate further through compilation, but no evidence here establishes such a path to the reported symbol-reference assertion.

Summary: This commit changes AArch64 GlobalISel outgoing-call lowering for Darwin by removing a special AnyExt transformation for AExt-assigned stack arguments. The accompanying AArch64 calling-convention tests update expected MIR for stack-passed narrow arguments, varargs, and aggregate calls.
Changed symbols: OutgoingArgHandler; AArch64CallLowering; test_stack_ext_needed; test_varargs; caller_s128; i8i16caller
Behavioral change: Outgoing argument lowering no longer forcibly applies buildAnyExt to an AExt argument before stack assignment.; Sub-64-bit Darwin stack-argument lowering is expected to preserve the appropriate stored width and stack layout rather than uniformly widening via the removed special case.; Regression expectations are updated for normal AArch64 and iOS/Darwin GlobalISel calling-convention MIR, including narrow stack arguments and varargs.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64
Reproducer link: The tests exercise GlobalISel call argument lowering and Darwin stack layout; the issue reproducer instead involves XRay patchable-function-entry metadata and an Assembly Printer MCSymbolRefExpr assertion.

Summary: This commit centralizes the requirement that alias queries involve memory instructions in MachineInstr::mayAlias and removes the AArch64 load/store optimizer's local mayAlias wrapper. AArch64LoadStoreOpt callers now invoke MachineInstr::mayAlias directly after their existing store checks.
Changed symbols: MachineInstr::mayAlias; AArch64LoadStoreOpt::findMatchingStore; AArch64LoadStoreOptimizer::mayAlias
Behavioral change: MachineInstr::mayAlias now returns false if either instruction is not a load or store, enforcing the memory-operation precondition centrally.; The AArch64 load/store optimizer removes its local alias helper and calls MachineInstr::mayAlias directly with TBAA disabled.; The prior local helper's memory-operation check only rejected the case where both instructions were non-memory operations; the centralized check rejects aliasing when either operand is non-memory.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64
Reproducer link: The retrieved change concerns AArch64 machine-instruction alias analysis, not XRay patchable-function-entry metadata or table emission.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64LoadStoreOptimizer; MachineInstr alias analysis
Causal explanation: There is a target-level overlap because the change affects AArch64 code generation, but the modified path is load/store optimization and MachineInstr alias analysis. The reported failure is an MCSymbolRefExpr/Symbol assertion during AArch64 Assembly Printer XRay-table emission. No retrieved hunk connects this alias-query behavior to XRay sled creation, MC symbol references, emitXRayTable, or patchable-function-entry lowering, so the causal link is weak.

evidence: Directly modifies AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable, the emission routine named by the issue.
Introduces PC-relative MCSymbolRefExpr and MCBinaryExpr symbol-difference emission for XRay sled and function table fields, matching the reported MCSymbolRefExpr/Symbol assertion mechanism.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Changes XRay sled version-2 table encoding from absolute symbol values to PC-relative expressions and updates XRay instrumentation-map handling for version-2 addresses. In AsmPrinter, XRay table entries are emitted directly as MC expressions relative to the table entry location, while the legacy path continues to emit absolute sled and current-function symbol values.
Changed symbols: AsmPrinter::XRayFunctionEntry::emit; AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable; InstrumentationMap::loadObj
Behavioral change: Simplifies XRayFunctionEntry::emit by removing its Location and CurrentFnSym inputs and changing it to emit through the caller-selected table format.; For the version-2 path in emitXRayTable, emits the sled address as Sled.Sled - Dot.; For the version-2 path, emits the function address as CurrentFnBegin - (Dot + WordSizeBytes), making the second field PC-relative from its own table location.; Retains an alternate legacy path that emits absolute Sled.Sled and CurrentFnSym values.; Instrumentation-map loading recognizes version-2 entries and adjusts decoded Address and Function values using the sled entry's location and word-size offset.
Assertion or trace link: Directly modifies AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable.; Directly constructs MCSymbolRefExpr instances for Sled.Sled, Dot, and CurrentFnBegin.; Directly passes MCBinaryExpr expressions to MCStreamer::emitValueImpl.; The issue signal explicitly includes MCSymbolRefExpr, Symbol assertion failure, AArch64 Assembly Printer, and emitXRayTable.
Reproducer link: The reported reduced AArch64 IR reaches XRay patchable-function-entry table emission; this change alters exactly how XRay sled and function symbols are represented in that emitted table.; The candidate's version-2 PC-relative encoding adds symbol-difference expressions involving the table-location symbol Dot, which is a plausible trigger point for an MC symbol/reference assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM CodeGen AsmPrinter; XRay table emission; LLVM MC expression and symbol-reference handling; XRay InstrumentationMap object decoding
Causal explanation: This is a strong candidate because it directly changes the XRay emission routine named in the issue and introduces MCSymbolRefExpr/MCBinaryExpr construction for XRay table fields. Although the candidate does not modify an AArch64-specific file, AArch64 uses the shared AsmPrinter XRay path, so an AArch64 llc crash while emitting patchable-function-entry/XRay metadata is consistent with this change. The older AArch64 CallLowering hunks are context only and are not evidence of a change in this candidate.
Causal confidence: 0.86
Build risk: Changes shared AsmPrinter object-emission behavior rather than only llvm-xray tooling.; Version-2 XRay tables depend on correct MC symbol ownership, symbol-difference legality, relocation generation, and table-field offsets.; No retrieved first-parent regression test specifically covers AArch64 XRay patchable-function-entry emission or the reported assertion.

top_candidates.subject: [XRay] Change Sled.Function to PC-relative for sled version 2 and make llvm-xray support sled version 2 addresses
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Changes XRay sled version-2 table encoding from absolute symbol values to PC-relative expressions and updates XRay instrumentation-map handling for version-2 addresses. In AsmPrinter, XRay table entries are emitted directly as MC expressions relative to the table entry location, while the legacy path continues to emit absolute sled and current-function symbol values.
Changed symbols: AsmPrinter::XRayFunctionEntry::emit; AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable; InstrumentationMap::loadObj
Behavioral change: Simplifies XRayFunctionEntry::emit by removing its Location and CurrentFnSym inputs and changing it to emit through the caller-selected table format.; For the version-2 path in emitXRayTable, emits the sled address as Sled.Sled - Dot.; For the version-2 path, emits the function address as CurrentFnBegin - (Dot + WordSizeBytes), making the second field PC-relative from its own table location.; Retains an alternate legacy path that emits absolute Sled.Sled and CurrentFnSym values.; Instrumentation-map loading recognizes version-2 entries and adjusts decoded Address and Function values using the sled entry's location and word-size offset.
Assertion or trace link: Directly modifies AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable.; Directly constructs MCSymbolRefExpr instances for Sled.Sled, Dot, and CurrentFnBegin.; Directly passes MCBinaryExpr expressions to MCStreamer::emitValueImpl.; The issue signal explicitly includes MCSymbolRefExpr, Symbol assertion failure, AArch64 Assembly Printer, and emitXRayTable.
Reproducer link: The reported reduced AArch64 IR reaches XRay patchable-function-entry table emission; this change alters exactly how XRay sled and function symbols are represented in that emitted table.; The candidate's version-2 PC-relative encoding adds symbol-difference expressions involving the table-location symbol Dot, which is a plausible trigger point for an MC symbol/reference assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM CodeGen AsmPrinter; XRay table emission; LLVM MC expression and symbol-reference handling; XRay InstrumentationMap object decoding

The older AArch64 CallLowering hunks are context only and are not evidence of a change in this candidate.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Adds Flang CHARACTER-comparison runtime helpers. The new templated comparison logic compares common prefixes, handles character kinds with different element widths, and applies Fortran blank-padding semantics to unequal-length strings.

Summary: Changes XRay sled version-2 table encoding to emit PC-relative values from AsmPrinter and adjusts XRay map loading for the revised addresses. In particular, XRay table emission now directly builds MC expressions for sled and function deltas, while retaining absolute symbol-value emission in the alternate path.
Changed symbols: llvm::AsmPrinter::XRayFunctionEntry::emit; llvm::AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable; llvm::xray::loadObj
Behavioral change: Changes XRayFunctionEntry::emit from a four-argument interface that accepted a location expression and current-function symbol to a two-argument interface taking only byte width and streamer.; Moves XRay table field emission into emitXRayTable and, in the shown PC-relative path, emits Sled.Sled - Dot as an MC binary expression.; Emits the function reference as CurrentFnBegin - (Dot + WordSizeBytes), making the second table word PC-relative to its own table location.; Uses MCSymbolRefExpr::create for Sled.Sled, CurrentFnBegin, and Dot when constructing the new emitted expressions; the alternate path emits absolute Sled.Sled and CurrentFnSym symbol values.; Adds initialization of a local Address value in XRay instrumentation-map object loading.

Summary: Adds Flang CHARACTER-comparison runtime helpers. The new templated comparison logic compares common prefixes, handles character kinds with different element widths, and applies Fortran blank-padding semantics to unequal-length strings.
Changed symbols: Fortran::runtime::CompareToBlankPadding; Fortran::runtime::Compare
Behavioral change: Introduces blank-padding comparison for remaining CHARACTER elements after the common-length prefix.; Uses memcmp for one-byte characters but element-wise comparison for char16_t and char32_t to avoid incorrect little-endian byte ordering.; Returns normalized comparison results of -1, 0, or 1 for CHARACTER scalar comparisons using the new helpers.
